headline: Brent fell to about $94 on US–Iran deal hopes, but Hormuz stays largely shut amid new strikes and IRGC mine claims. North Korea fired missiles on 4 Nov; Democrats won both houses of Congress.

situations.name: US–Iran war and Gulf energy shock
situations.summary: Trump confirmed strikes on Iranian air defences; Iran called the US reply on Hormuz unconvincing on 4 Nov. Brent fell to about $94 on deal hopes.

situations.name: Russia–Ukraine war and NATO's flank
situations.summary: Toll from 2 Nov strike on a Zaporizhzhia aid point reached 33; Russian strikes on 3 Nov cut power widely. Talks set for 10–11 Nov.

situations.name: Super El Niño
situations.summary: ONI rose to +2.5 for Aug–Oct: drought risk in East and southern Africa, record-range warmth and faster CO₂ growth.

situations.name: Ebola outbreak, DR Congo
situations.summary: Africa CDC counted 5,376 Ebola deaths among more than 10,000 cases to 2 Nov, mostly in DR Congo; a WHO emergency (PHEIC) since May.

situations.name: Sudan war
situations.summary: Drone strikes have cut parts of Sudan off the power grid; a strike on a South Kordofan fuel station killed 10 on 4 Nov.

situations.name: Cyclone Murasu
situations.summary: Murasu crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole on 3 Nov and weakened inland; two dead and 12,230 people moved to relief centres.

situations.name: France: debt stress and protests
situations.summary: OAT–Bund spread near 160bp on 2 Nov; budget vote delayed and unions hold a general strike on 5 Nov.

situations.name: Energy shock feeding inflation
situations.summary: US CPI 4.0%; Australia hiked to 4.85% on 3 Nov and a Bank of England rise to 4% is expected on 5 Nov.

situations.name: Binance theft and North Korean escalation
situations.summary: FBI blames North Korea for a $6.3bn Binance theft; Pyongyang denied it and fired missiles on 4 Nov. Binance withdrawals are resuming.

signals.name: US equity stress
signals.summary: VIX back below 20 and S&P 500 1.4% off its high after Democrats win Congress
signals.state: The VIX was near 17.1 on 4 Nov, back below the 20 Watch line, and the S&P 500 was about 1.4% below its 52-week high (Yahoo Finance). Democrats won control of both the House and Senate in the 3 Nov midterms, removing an event risk markets had hedged (Time). The Bank of England (5 Nov) and US payrolls (6 Nov) are the next scheduled tests.
signals.for_you: Equity markets are calm by this measure. Pension and investment values that track US shares are near recent highs; conditions can change quickly around central bank decisions and data releases.
signals.rubric_hit: VIX 17.1 < 20 and S&P drawdown 1.4% < 5% = Normal

signals.for_you: UK shares are steady; pensions and ISAs tracking the index are close to recent highs.

signals.summary: Treasury volatility at the 100 Watch line; 10-year yield near 4.95%

The Treasury's quarterly refunding (4 Nov) and October payrolls (6 Nov) are the next tests.
signals.for_you: Higher and more volatile bond yields feed through to mortgage and loan rates, particularly in the US.

signals.summary: Gold near $4,050, down 7.9% over three months, just inside the Normal band
signals.state: Gold futures were near $4,052 at 11:30 UK on 4 Nov, up 0.5% over the week and 7.9% lower over three months, back inside the 8% fall Watch line after dipping past it earlier in the day. They remain about 24% below their 52-week high. Recent weakness reflects higher yields and expected rate rises rather than a flight to safety.
signals.for_you: Gold is no longer signalling unusual stress on its three-month move. Prices remain well below their peak, which affects holders of gold and gold-linked savings.

signals.name: Crypto stress
signals.summary: Bitcoin 7% off its high; Binance withdrawals resuming after record theft
signals.state: Bitcoin was near $80,200 on 4 Nov, about 7% below its 52-week high and far from the 25% Watch line (Yahoo Finance). Binance restored withdrawals for major coins from 1 Nov and plans to cover most of the roughly $6bn theft the FBI attributes to North Korea (CBS News). With outflows reported as normalised and no stablecoin de-peg, exchange stress no longer meets the Watch line as of 4 Nov.
signals.for_you: Crypto holders face normal volatility. Exchange-specific risk remains after the Binance theft; regulators' consumer warnings on crypto still apply.
signals.rubric_hit: BTC drawdown 7% < 25%; no top-10 exchange failing = Normal

signals.state: SOFR peaked 5bp above the Fed's interest on reserves in the five days to 2 Nov, inside the 10bp Watch line, and Fed overnight repo operations were near zero to 3 Nov. Money markets show no sign of a dollar shortage as of 4 Nov.
signals.for_you: No knock-on effects for households; funding stress would show up first in bank and market borrowing costs.

signals.name: Private credit stress
signals.value: Q3 BDC requests ~11.5% of NAV vs 5% caps
signals.summary: Non-traded BDC redemption requests still far above 5% caps; gates remain in force
signals.state: Non-traded BDCs received Q3 redemption requests worth about 11.5% of NAV against typical 5% quarterly caps, leaving billions unmet (With Intelligence; iCapital). Blackstone's BCRED reported a 30 Sep NAV of $23.51 after paying about half of requests in Q2. No new large fund gate, forced sale or spillover to banks or insurers had been reported as of 4 Nov.
signals.for_you: Investors in semi-liquid private credit funds may be able to withdraw only part of what they ask for each quarter. Most savers' exposure is indirect, through pensions.

signals.state: Headline CPI rose 4.0% in the year to September, up from 3.7%, within the 3–4.5% Watch band (BLS via FRED). Brent fell to about $94 on 4 Nov, near a three-week low, on hopes of a US–Iran deal, which may ease energy inflation if sustained. October CPI is due mid-November.
signals.for_you: Prices are rising faster than the Fed's 2% target, squeezing real incomes. Fuel and energy costs are the main swing factor in coming months.

signals.name: Euro-area economy
signals.summary: Euro-area flash PMI eased to 51.9 in October; Q3 GDP grew 0.4%
signals.state: The HCOB euro-area flash composite PMI fell to 51.9 in October from September, below the 52.7 expected but still above 50 (S&P Global, 23 Oct). Eurostat's flash estimate on 30 Oct showed Q3 GDP up 0.4%, though French output contracted. Neither stagnation nor a sub-50 PMI is confirmed as of 4 Nov; the final October PMIs are due this week.
signals.for_you: Euro-area activity is still growing but slowing. Firms exposed to energy costs and French demand face the most pressure.
signals.rubric_hit: Composite PMI 51.9 > 50 and GDP positive = Normal

signals.name: China economy
signals.summary: Regulators pause IPOs to steady falling stocks; factory PMI in contraction
signals.state: Chinese regulators told banks to pause IPOs and large share sales to steady a falling stock market, the FT reported on 3 Nov (via Yahoo Finance). The official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October. Q3 GDP grew 4.5%, near target, with no sign of financial contagion or tighter capital controls as of 4 Nov.
signals.for_you: Weaker Chinese demand can weigh on commodity exporters and firms selling into China. No financial contagion is visible.
signals.rubric_hit: Growth near target; no contagion or capital controls = Normal

signals.name: Central bank stress
signals.summary: Bank of England widely expected to raise rates on 5 Nov; RBA hiked on 3 Nov
signals.state: The Bank of England is widely expected to raise Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023, as the energy shock lifts inflation (Yahoo Finance; HomeOwners Alliance). Australia's central bank raised its cash rate to 4.85% on 3 Nov. The Fed held at 3.75–4% on 28 Oct. Policymakers face a stagflationary dilemma; no emergency move had been made as of 4 Nov.
signals.for_you: Borrowers on variable or expiring fixed-rate loans are most exposed to rising rates; savers may see better returns. Lenders often reprice products after decisions.
signals.rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma across major central banks = Watch

signals.summary: France–Bund spread near 160bp, above the 150bp Alert line; general strike on 5 Nov
signals.state: France's 10-year spread over German Bunds was 159.9bp on 2 Nov, after peaking at 174.6bp on 22 Oct, and the OAT yield was just under 4.9% on 4 Nov (Journal du Coin; Trading Economics). The vote on the 2027 budget's revenue side has been postponed twice, with a deadline of 17 Nov, and unions strike on 5 Nov. No failed auction or emergency ECB buying has been reported.
signals.for_you: Higher French borrowing costs can feed into euro-area mortgage and business lending rates. Holders of French bonds or funds that own them are most exposed to price swings.

signals.value: Lira, Egyptian pound at record lows
signals.summary: Turkish lira and Egyptian pound at record lows; no major EM default or capital controls
signals.state: The Turkish lira hit a new record low on 4 Nov, near 50 per dollar, in a gradual slide (Izvestia; Benzinga). Egypt's pound passed 56 per dollar in late October, a record low, as foreign funds sold local debt (Reuters via MarketScreener). Neither has lost more than 10% in a month, and no major emerging economy had defaulted or imposed capital controls as of 4 Nov.
signals.for_you: Travellers and importers dealing in these currencies face shifting exchange rates. No acute emerging-market crisis is under way.

signals.name: Oil (Brent)
signals.summary: Brent near $94 on deal hopes, but Hormuz remains largely shut to shipping
signals.state: Brent fell to about $94 on 4 Nov, down about 18% in a week, as Democrats won Congress and talks on a US–Iran deal continued (Yahoo Finance; ProtoThema). The price alone is in the Watch band, but Alert holds on the physical outage: Hormuz is still largely closed, and Iran says it will reopen the strait within two days only if the US meets its demands, including ending the naval blockade (Al Jazeera, 4 Nov).
signals.for_you: Fuel and heating costs follow crude with a lag, so recent falls may take weeks to reach pump prices. Prices could move sharply either way on news from the Gulf.
signals.rubric_hit: Major physical supply outage (Hormuz largely shut, >2 mb/d) = Alert; Brent $94 alone = Watch

signals.name: Critical minerals
signals.summary: China's rare-earth export-control pause expires 10 Nov with no renewal announced
signals.state: China's one-year suspension of its October 2025 rare-earth export controls, including the 0.1% content rule, expires on 10 Nov, and no renewal had been announced as of 4 Nov (FXStreet; China Briefing). Lapsed controls would bring back tighter licensing. No production stoppages outside China have been confirmed, so the Alert line is not crossed.
signals.for_you: Manufacturers relying on rare-earth magnets, such as carmakers and electronics firms, are most exposed to licensing delays if the pause lapses.

signals.value: Hormuz closed to Gulf urea exports
signals.summary: Gulf urea exports still stuck behind Hormuz in the conflict's ninth month
signals.state: Hormuz, the route for about a third of world urea exports, remains largely closed (Global Agriculture, 30 Oct; IFPRI). US retail urea was $674 a ton in mid-October, 13% higher than a year earlier, as Chinese exports offset some of the loss. A key export route closed meets the Alert line; the IRGC's 4 Nov mine claims add to the risk.
signals.for_you: Farmers face higher fertiliser costs, which can feed into food prices next season. Import-dependent countries in South Asia and Africa are most exposed.

signals.summary: Zaporizhzhia relies on one power line as Russia strikes Ukraine's energy system
signals.state: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant has depended on a single off-site line since repairs after an 18-day loss of off-site power, in a ceasefire window the IAEA brokered (Al Jazeera; World Nuclear News). Russian strikes on 3 Nov hit energy sites across Ukraine and left large areas without power (Outlook India). No damage to safety systems has been reported as of 4 Nov.
signals.for_you: No public health action is needed. Follow official national and IAEA updates if travelling to or living near affected regions.
signals.rubric_hit: Plant reliant on a single off-site line amid strikes = Watch; no safety-system damage

signals.summary: Indonesia deploys 21,000 troops in Jakarta after generals' arrest; Democrats win US Congress
signals.state: Indonesian police detained three senior police generals, including the president's chief of staff, over alleged wiretapping of President Prabowo, and the military is deploying about 21,000 personnel to Jakarta; officials call it routine (AP via ABC News, 4 Nov). Democrats won both chambers in the 3 Nov US midterms, an uncontested result (Time). No G20 government had fallen and no coup was reported as of 4 Nov.
signals.for_you: Check FCDO travel advice for Indonesia and France before travelling; large deployments or strikes can disrupt transport.

signals.name: Europe hybrid attacks
signals.summary: Supermarket refrigeration attacks hit stores in several EU states; no claim or attribution
signals.state: Cyberattacks on 2 Nov caused fridges and freezers to fail at more than 100 shops in several EU countries, including Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden and Ireland; Belgian prosecutors opened a criminal investigation and the EU agriculture commissioner called it a deliberate attempt to disrupt food supply (Al Jazeera, 3 Nov). Nobody has claimed the attacks and no state has been formally blamed.
signals.for_you: Food safety is not reported at risk; follow shop and Food Standards Agency advice if products are withdrawn.

signals.value: 33 killed at aid site; 289 drones 3 Nov
signals.summary: Toll from Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia aid point reaches 33; mass drone and missile strikes
signals.state: The toll from the 2 Nov Russian guided-bomb strike on people collecting aid in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, rose to 33 on 3 Nov, with dozens missing (Ukrainska Pravda). Overnight into 3 Nov Russia launched 289 drones and 17 ballistic missiles at energy sites and a Kharkiv medical facility, Zelensky said (Euronews). US-mediated working-level talks are planned for 10–11 Nov in Abu Dhabi.
signals.for_you: Follow FCDO advice against all travel to Ukraine. Energy-market effects are indirect.

signals.summary: Drone strikes cripple Sudan's power grid; fuel station strike kills 10 in South Kordofan
signals.state: Drone strikes blamed on the RSF have hit Sudan's largest thermal plant and several substations since late October, cutting White Nile and North Kordofan off the grid (AP, 2 Nov). A drone strike on a fuel station in South Kordofan killed more than 10 civilians on 4 Nov (Darfur24; Sudan Tribune). The IPC warns of a growing risk of famine in Darfur and Kordofan; no talks are under way.

signals.name: Famine
signals.summary: IPC warns of growing famine risk in Darfur and Kordofan; El Niño threatens Somalia
signals.state: An IPC alert on 12 Oct warned of a growing risk of famine in parts of Greater Darfur and Greater Kordofan in Sudan, where drought affects about half the country (WHO). The IPC's Somalia analysis projects worsening food insecurity for October–December. No current IPC Phase 5 classification was confirmed as of 4 Nov.
signals.for_you: Aid agencies' appeals are the main route for public support.

signals.name: Forced displacement
signals.summary: No new event displacing 500,000; Moyale fighting sends 50,000 into Kenya
signals.state: No single new event displacing more than 500,000 people in a month had been found as of 4 Nov. Fighting in Moyale, Ethiopia, has sent more than 50,000 people into Kenya since late October (allAfrica, 4 Nov). UNHCR's winter appeal says 9 million people need winter aid.
signals.for_you: Aid agencies' appeals are the main route for public support.

signals.name: Civil unrest
signals.summary: France braces for 5 Nov general strike after weeks of mass protests and arrests
signals.state: French unions and all four major rail unions have called a general strike for 5 Nov after the government offered no concessions (Latin Times; Sortiraparis). About 410,000 marched on 24 Oct with 1,314 arrests and around 50 officers injured; no deaths have been reported. Indonesia deployed about 21,000 troops in Jakarta on 4 Nov, with no protests reported (AP).
signals.for_you: Expect transport and school disruption in France on 5 Nov; check operators and FCDO travel advice.
signals.rubric_hit: Significant protests in several countries = Watch; no deadly nationwide unrest

signals.name: Humanitarian funding gap
signals.summary: Humanitarian appeals badly underfunded; WFP cut Gaza food aid for 500,000
signals.state: WHO's Sudan health appeal was only 23% funded as of mid-October (WHO, 12 Oct), and WFP cut monthly food aid in Gaza from 1.6 million to 1.1 million people from late October after receiving less than half its usual funding. UNHCR's winter appeal warns resources are dwindling. No new pipeline break was reported as of 4 Nov.
signals.for_you: Aid agencies' appeals are the main route for public support.

signals.name: UK inflation & rates
signals.summary: UK inflation 3.5%; Bank of England expected to raise Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov
signals.state: UK CPI inflation rose to 3.5% in September, within the 2.5–4.0% Watch band. The Bank of England is widely expected to raise Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023, as the energy shock lifts inflation (Yahoo Finance; HomeOwners Alliance).
signals.for_you: Mortgage holders on tracker or expiring fixed deals are most exposed to a rate rise; savings rates may edge up.

signals.name: Gilt market
signals.summary: 10-year gilt yield near 5.2% ahead of an expected rate rise on 5 Nov
signals.state: The 10-year gilt yield fell to about 5.3% on 2 Nov and was near 5.2% on 3 Nov, below its October high near 5.4%, a multi-year peak (Trading Economics). A Bank of England rise, its first since 2023, is widely expected on 5 Nov. Auctions have been orderly as of 4 Nov.
signals.for_you: High gilt yields keep fixed mortgage rates elevated; borrowers remortgaging soon are most exposed.
signals.rubric_hit: Gilt yields near multi-decade highs = Watch; no BoE intervention

signals.name: UK energy price cap
signals.summary: Energy cap £1,723; January forecasts range from +16% to +27%
signals.state: The Ofgem cap for October–December is £1,723 a year. Cornwall Insight's latest forecast puts January at £1,999, up 16%, while some supplier-based forecasts point to about +27% (Cornwall Insight; Energy Made Easy). Alert is held under hysteresis until Ofgem announces the January cap by 25 Nov; Brent fell to about $94 on 4 Nov.
signals.for_you: Households on default tariffs face a likely rise in January. Ofgem's guidance explains how the cap works and where to get help with bills.
signals.rubric_hit: Forecast rise 16–27% straddles the 20% Alert line; held pending Ofgem
